context.body: Selected for the reader trail because “Darkness, the Aramaic cry, a torn veil, and witnesses at a distance” preserves a distinct parallel witness source unit within death witness.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Darkness extends from the sixth hour to the ninth before Jesus’ preserved Aramaic cry.
observations.label: Darkness, the Aramaic cry, a torn veil, and witnesses at a distance: textual observation

observations.body: The cry is translated; bystanders hear Elijah; the centurion names Jesus after seeing how he died.
observations.label: Darkness, the Aramaic cry, a torn veil, and witnesses at a distance: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: The centurion stands opposite Jesus while named women watch from a distance.
observations.label: Relationships named in Mark 15:33–41

payload.posture: Read Mark 15:33–41 as its own death, signs, and witnesses crucifixion setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The same death is observed from opposite and distant positions, and the observers do not voice the same response.
payload.title: Darkness, the Aramaic cry, a torn veil, and witnesses at a distance
